tips.title: Math Learning Tips
tips.intro: Master these tips to help children improve their mental math skills more effectively:
tips.tip1Desc: Begin with a small number range (1-10) for addition and subtraction. Build confidence before increasing difficulty.
tips.tip2Desc: 10-15 minutes of daily practice is more effective than occasional long sessions. Consistency is key.
tips.tip3Desc: Encourage children to understand the nature of operations rather than just memorizing formulas. For example, multiplication is repeated addition.
tips.tip4Desc: Comparison exercises help children develop number sense and understand relationships between numbers.
tips.tip5Desc: Master one operation before introducing the next. Suggested order: Addition → Subtraction → Multiplication → Division.
tips.tip6Desc: Give plenty of positive feedback. Focus on progress rather than mistakes to keep children motivated.

glossary.title: Math Glossary
glossary.description: Elementary math terms with definitions to help children understand mathematical vocabulary.
glossary.intro: A collection of common math terms used in elementary school. Use the search to find specific terms.

addend.definition: A number being added in an addition operation. In 3 + 5 = 8, both 3 and 5 are addends.

difference.definition: The result of a subtraction operation. In 8 - 3 = 5, the difference is 5.

dividend.definition: The number being divided in a division operation. In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the dividend is 12.

divisor.definition: The number by which another number is divided. In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the divisor is 3.

equal.definition: A symbol showing that two values are the same.

equation.definition: A mathematical statement with an equal sign showing two expressions have the same value. Example: 2 + 3 = 5.

factor.definition: A number being multiplied in a multiplication operation. In 3 × 4 = 12, both 3 and 4 are factors.

greaterThan.definition: Shows that the number on the left is larger than the number on the right. Example: 5 > 3.

lessThan.definition: Shows that the number on the left is smaller than the number on the right. Example: 3 < 5.

minuend.definition: The number from which another number is subtracted. In 8 - 3 = 5, the minuend is 8.

multiplicand.definition: The number being multiplied in a multiplication operation. In 3 × 4 = 12, the multiplicand is 3.

multiplier.definition: The number by which another number is multiplied. In 3 × 4 = 12, the multiplier is 4.

numberLine.definition: A straight line with numbers marked on it, used to show the size and order of numbers.

product.definition: The result of a multiplication operation. In 3 × 4 = 12, the product is 12.

quotient.definition: The result of a division operation. In 12 ÷ 3 = 4, the quotient is 4.

remainder.definition: The amount left over after division when numbers don't divide evenly. Example: 10 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 1.

subtrahend.definition: The number being subtracted in a subtraction operation. In 8 - 3 = 5, the subtrahend is 3.

sum.definition: The result of an addition operation. In 3 + 5 = 8, the sum is 8.

guide.title: Parent's Guide
guide.description: Tips and advice for parents on helping children learn math effectively.
guide.intro: Math learning isn't just about school — parental involvement and guidance are equally important. Here are some tips to help you support your child.

creatingEnvironment.title: Creating a Learning Environment
creatingEnvironment.item1: Prepare a quiet, organized study space for your child with minimal distractions.
creatingEnvironment.item2: Place math-related books and cards around the home for easy access.
creatingEnvironment.item3: Maintain a positive attitude and avoid showing anxiety about math in front of your child.

effectivePractice.title: Effective Practice Methods
effectivePractice.item1: 10-15 minutes of daily practice is more effective than occasional long sessions.
effectivePractice.item2: Start simple and gradually increase difficulty to build confidence.
effectivePractice.item3: Encourage your child to explain their thinking process, not just the answer.
effectivePractice.item4: Use the Daily Challenge feature to build a daily practice habit.

handlingMistakes.title: Handling Mistakes
handlingMistakes.item1: Mistakes are part of learning — don't scold your child for getting answers wrong.
handlingMistakes.item2: Guide your child to analyze why they made the mistake and learn from it.
handlingMistakes.item3: Use the wrong answer book feature to regularly review challenging problems.

motivation.title: Motivation & Encouragement
motivation.item1: Focus on your child's progress rather than comparing with others.
motivation.item2: Set small goals and give appropriate rewards and praise when achieved.
motivation.item3: Make math fun through games, stories, and other engaging activities.

ageAppropriate.title: Age-Appropriate Suggestions
ageAppropriate.item1: Preschool (4-6): Focus on addition and subtraction within 1-10 to build number sense.
ageAppropriate.item2: Lower grades (1-3): Master addition and subtraction within 20, begin learning multiplication tables.
ageAppropriate.item3: Upper grades (4-6): Consolidate four operations, start exploring fractions and decimals.

dailyLife.title: Math in Daily Life
dailyLife.item1: Let your child calculate prices and change while shopping to practice real-world math.
dailyLife.item2: Involve your child in measuring ingredients while cooking to understand fractions and ratios.
dailyLife.item3: Have your child read signs and calculate distances during outings to develop number sense.
